    <briefdescription>
<para>Accumulates set-bit counts across <computeroutput><ref refid="classsimd__mask" kindref="compound">simd_mask</ref>&lt;V&gt;</computeroutput> instances. </para>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para>Folds a sequence of masks into a running total reported by <computeroutput>result()</computeroutput>.</para>
<sect1 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md66_1s1"><sect2 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md66">
<title>Overflow</title><para><computeroutput>count()</computeroutput> performs no overflow check. The maximum number of <computeroutput>count()</computeroutput> calls a single instance absorbs without wrap is <computeroutput>portion_size()</computeroutput>. Beyond that bound, lane accumulation wraps in two&apos;s-complement arithmetic. To process more than <computeroutput>portion_size()</computeroutput> masks, construct a fresh <computeroutput><ref refid="classcounter" kindref="compound">counter</ref>&lt;V&gt;</computeroutput> per portion and accumulate <computeroutput>result()</computeroutput> into a wider scalar.</para>
</sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md67_1s1"><sect2 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md67">
<title>State</title><para>No reset operation. <computeroutput>result()</computeroutput> does not modify state.</para>
</sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md68_1s1"><sect2 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md68">
<title>Template Parameters</title><para><parameterlist kind="templateparam"><parameteritem>
<parameternamelist>
<parametername>V</parametername>
</parameternamelist>
<parameterdescription>
<para>Vector type providing <computeroutput>mask_type</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>value_type</computeroutput>. Constraint: <computeroutput>trivially_chunk_swappable</computeroutput>.</para>
</parameterdescription>
</parameteritem>
</parameterlist>
</para>
</sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md69_1s1"><sect2 id="classcounter_1autotoc_md69">
<title>Type aliases</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><computeroutput>value_type</computeroutput> — <computeroutput>V::value_type</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>mask_type</computeroutput> — <computeroutput>V::mask_type</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>index_type</computeroutput> — <computeroutput>IntegerForSizeof&lt;value_type&gt;::Signed</computeroutput>. </para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect2></sect1>
    </detaileddescription>

    </sectiondef>
    <briefdescription>
<para>A fixed-size SIMD vector abstraction with ISA/ABI‑aware backend dispatch. </para>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para>The <computeroutput><ref refid="classraze_1_1vx_1_1simd" kindref="compound">simd</ref></computeroutput> class provides a high-level, type-safe interface for performing vectorized arithmetic, logical, comparison, and shift operations across multiple hardware instruction sets (SSE2, SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX‑512, etc.). It wraps architecture-specific intrinsic types and exposes a uniform API that behaves consistently across all supported ABIs.</para>
<sect1 id="classraze_1_1vx_1_1simd_1autotoc_md75_1s1"><sect2 id="classraze_1_1vx_1_1simd_1autotoc_md75">
<title>Key Characteristics</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Represents a vector of <computeroutput>value_type</computeroutput> elements stored in a native SIMD register.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>All operations are performed element-wise.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>

    </sectiondef>
    <briefdescription>
<para>A fixed-size SIMD mask with ISA/ABI-aware backend dispatch. </para>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para><computeroutput><ref refid="classsimd__mask" kindref="compound">simd_mask</ref>&lt;T, Abi&gt;</computeroutput> is the mask counterpart of <computeroutput><ref refid="classraze_1_1vx_1_1simd" kindref="compound">raze::vx::simd</ref>&lt;T, Abi&gt;</computeroutput>. It has the same lane count as <computeroutput>simd&lt;T, Abi&gt;</computeroutput> and is used as the operand type for masked overloads of vector primitives and algorithms, e.g.:</para>
<para><programlisting filename=".cpp"><codeline><highlight class="keyword">auto</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>m<sp/>=<sp/>(a<sp/>&lt;<sp/>b);<sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/></highlight><highlight class="comment">//<sp/>simd_mask</highlight><highlight class="normal"></highlight></codeline>
<codeline><highlight class="normal"></highlight><highlight class="keyword">auto</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>r<sp/>=<sp/><ref refid="group__raze__vx__arith_1ga214030e230044f68af4225899a4b79be" kindref="member">raze::vx::add</ref>[m](a,<sp/>b);<sp/><sp/></highlight><highlight class="comment">//<sp/>masked<sp/>add</highlight></codeline>
</programlisting></para>
<para>A mask stores one boolean per lane. The in-register representation is ABI-dependent (byte masks on SSE/AVX2, <computeroutput>k</computeroutput>-registers on AVX-512), but the public interface is uniform and lane-indexed.</para>
<sect1 id="classsimd__mask_1autotoc_md70_1s1"><sect2 id="classsimd__mask_1autotoc_md70">
<title>Key Characteristics</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Same lane count as the corresponding <computeroutput>simd&lt;T, Abi&gt;</computeroutput> (<computeroutput><ref refid="classsimd__mask_1ad1ddfada301856a30b99b6312c46b0bd" kindref="member">size()</ref></computeroutput>).</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Default-constructs to all-false</bold>, unlike <computeroutput>simd</computeroutput> which leaves lanes uninitialized. Use <computeroutput><ref refid="classsimd__mask" kindref="compound">simd_mask(uninitialized)</ref></computeroutput> to skip initialization.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>Boolean operations (<computeroutput>&amp;</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>|</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>^</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>!</computeroutput>) and comparisons (<computeroutput>==</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>!=</computeroutput>) operate element-wise and return <computeroutput><ref refid="classsimd__mask" kindref="compound">simd_mask</ref></computeroutput>, not <computeroutput>bool</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect2></sect1>

=== conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion.xml ===
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='no'?>
<doxygen xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="compound.xsd" version="1.18.0" xml:lang="en-US">
  <compounddef id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion" kind="concept">
    <compoundname>raze::vx::supports_fast_conversion</compoundname>
    <includes local="no">C:/Users/danya/source/repos/Midoritotoro/raze/src/raze/vx/hw/configurable/arithmetic/Convert.h</includes>
    <templateparamlist>
      <param>
        <type>class V</type>
      </param>
      <param>
        <type>class To</type>
      </param>
    </templateparamlist>
    <initializer>template&lt;class V, class To&gt;
concept <ref refid="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion" kindref="compound">raze::vx::supports_fast_conversion</ref> =  simd_type&lt;V&gt; &amp;&amp; arithmetic_type&lt;To&gt; &amp;&amp;
    (!compatibility::is_msvc_only || (((V::size() * sizeof(typename V::value_type)) &gt;= 16) &amp;&amp; ((V::size() * sizeof(To)) &gt;= 16)))</initializer>
    <conceptparts>
      <codepart line="262">    <programlisting>
<codeline><highlight class="keyword">template</highlight><highlight class="normal">&lt;</highlight><highlight class="keyword">class</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>V,<sp/></highlight><highlight class="keyword">class</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>To&gt;</highlight></codeline>
<codeline><highlight class="normal"></highlight><highlight class="keyword">concept<sp/></highlight><highlight class="normal">supports_fast_conversion<sp/>=<sp/>simd_type&lt;V&gt;<sp/>&amp;&amp;<sp/>arithmetic_type&lt;To&gt;<sp/>&amp;&amp;</highlight></codeline>
<codeline><highlight class="normal"><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/>(!compatibility::is_msvc_only<sp/>||<sp/>(((V::size()<sp/>*<sp/></highlight><highlight class="keyword">sizeof</highlight><highlight class="normal">(</highlight><highlight class="keyword">typename</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>V::value_type))<sp/>&gt;=<sp/>16)<sp/>&amp;&amp;<sp/>((V::size()<sp/>*<sp/></highlight><highlight class="keyword">sizeof</highlight><highlight class="normal">(To))<sp/>&gt;=<sp/>16)))</highlight></codeline>
    </programlisting>
</codepart>
    </conceptparts>
    <briefdescription>
<para>Heuristic hint: will <computeroutput>convert&lt;To&gt;</computeroutput> on this SIMD type emit native SIMD? </para>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para>Detects whether converting every lane of a SIMD value of type <computeroutput>V</computeroutput> to element type <computeroutput>To</computeroutput> is <bold>likely</bold> to be lowered to native SIMD instructions by the current compiler and ABI, or will degrade into per-lane scalar code.</para>
<sect1 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md150_1s1"><sect2 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md150_1s2"><sect3 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md150">
<title>What it actually checks</title><para>The check is deliberately conservative and platform-aware:</para>
<para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>MSVC</bold>: returns <computeroutput>true</computeroutput> only when <computeroutput>V</computeroutput> is guaranteed to occupy at least ones full hardware register (<computeroutput>sizeof(V) &gt;= 16</computeroutput>) <bold>and</bold> the destination type is at least register-wide (<computeroutput>V::size() * sizeof(To) &gt;= 16</computeroutput>). This is the minimum bar for MSVC to avoid <computeroutput>simd</computeroutput> being represented as a <emphasis>tuple of scalars</emphasis>, which forces the codegen into per-lane loops with mask-blends and register spills — the worst-case pathological output.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>GCC / Clang / ICPX</bold>: returns <computeroutput>true</computeroutput> unconditionally. These compilers have mature SIMD backends and a general-purpose vectorizer, so native SIMD lowering is the overwhelmingly common case — even when the check cannot prove it in advance.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md151_1s1"><sect2 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md151_1s2"><sect3 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md151">
<title>Caveats</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>&quot;Fast&quot; is subjective.</bold> This concept does <bold>not</bold> measure performance. It is a <emphasis>codegen heuristic</emphasis>, not a benchmark. A return value of <computeroutput>true</computeroutput> only means &quot;the compiler is likely to emit SIMD instructions&quot;, not &quot;this code path will be faster than scalar&quot;.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold><computeroutput>true</computeroutput> ≠ SIMD.</bold> Even on GCC/Clang/ICPX, some conversions on exotic types or unusual register widths may still fall back to scalar per-element loops. The concept is a <emphasis>hint to gate a manual fast-path</emphasis>, not a guarantee that the fast-path is engaged.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold><computeroutput>false</computeroutput> ≠ correctness issue.</bold> Returning <computeroutput>false</computeroutput> never means the conversion is wrong. It means &quot;the compiler is known to take a
     slow path&quot;, and the caller should let the algorithm use its own scalar fallback instead of forcing a half-vectorized middle ground.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md152_1s1"><sect2 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md152_1s2"><sect3 id="conceptraze_1_1vx_1_1supports__fast__conversion_1autotoc_md152">
<title>Why bother</title><para>On MSVC, gating a SIMD fast-path with this concept avoids the worst codegen (nested per-lane loops and spills inside the inner vector loop). On GCC/Clang/ICPX, the concept is almost always <computeroutput>true</computeroutput>, so it costs nothing in practice and keeps the code portable across compilers.</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>

=== dynamic_dispatch.xml ===
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='no'?>
<doxygen xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="compound.xsd" version="1.18.0" xml:lang="en-US">
  <compounddef id="dynamic_dispatch" kind="page">
    <compoundname>dynamic_dispatch</compoundname>
    <title>Dynamic dispatch in &lt;tt&gt;raze::algorithm&lt;/tt&gt;</title>
    <briefdescription>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para>Algorithms in <computeroutput>raze::algorithm</computeroutput> can adapt to the host CPU instruction set at runtime. However, the dispatch mechanism heavily depends on the target compiler and the available ISA.</para>
<sect1 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md85_1s1"><sect2 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md85_1s2"><sect3 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md85">
<title>Static Dispatch Override</title><para>Regardless of the compiler, if the target ISA at compile time (via <computeroutput>-march</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>/arch:</computeroutput>, or specific <computeroutput>-misa*</computeroutput> flags) already satisfies the reference ISA (the maximum ISA required by the algorithm&apos;s implementation), the algorithm will <bold>always</bold> use static dispatch. The runtime check is completely elided.</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md86_1s1"><sect2 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md86_1s2"><sect3 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md86">
<title>Mechanism</title><para>If the reference ISA is not guaranteed at compile time, the fallback behavior differs by compiler:</para>
<para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>MSVC</bold>: <bold>All</bold> algorithms use a hand-written explicit runtime dispatcher. CPU feature detection (e.g., via CPUID) is performed <bold>at program startup</bold>. The generated dispatcher then forwards execution to the most optimized implementation based on the detected features. There is no automatic compiler-driven dynamic dispatch for loops. To force static dispatch (using the compile-time target ISA), you must explicitly pass the <computeroutput>raze::options::fstatic</computeroutput> option.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>GCC / Clang</bold>: Dynamic dispatch is <bold>only</bold> applied to algorithms with loops that are easily auto-vectorizable by the compiler. For these, <computeroutput>__attribute__((target_clones))</computeroutput> is emitted, generating multiple versions of the loop. The runtime resolver selects the best version. More complex algorithms (e.g., those with complex dependencies or hard-to-vectorize predicates) may not receive dynamic dispatch and will rely on the compile-time ISA.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md87_1s1"><sect2 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md87_1s2"><sect3 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md87">
<title>Affected Algorithms</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>MSVC</bold>: Every algorithm supports runtime dispatch.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>GCC / Clang</bold>: Primarily simple map-style algorithms and linear traversals where the hot loop is entirely inlined and easily cloned:<itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><computeroutput>for_each</computeroutput></para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>transform</computeroutput></para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>replace</computeroutput></para>
</listitem><listitem><para>and similar element-wise range operations.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md88_1s1"><sect2 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md88_1s2"><sect3 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md88">
<title>Performance Characteristics</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>Zero API changes</bold>: Call the algorithm as usual.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Overhead</bold>: The runtime resolution adds a negligible one-time cost (or a highly predictable branch per call, depending on the compiler). For very short ranges, the dispatch overhead may outweigh the SIMD benefit.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Code bloat</bold>: Expect the binary size to increase slightly, as multiple copies of the inner loop exist for different ISAs.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md89_1s1"><sect2 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md89_1s2"><sect3 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md89">
<title>Interplay with Options</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>If <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__options_1ga6e41c5c8d3ba0dbed249b7d479100116" kindref="member">fscalar</ref></computeroutput> is used, the vectorized paths are bypassed entirely, degenerating to a scalar implementation regardless of the CPU capabilities.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>If <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__options_1gadd76b44edfe6913f42caaef657772975" kindref="member">fstatic</ref></computeroutput> is used, dynamic dispatch is disabled, and the algorithm relies strictly on the compile-time target ISA.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md90_1s1"><sect2 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md90_1s2"><sect3 id="dynamic_dispatch_1autotoc_md90">
<title>See also</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><ref refid="mask_semantics" kindref="compound">Mask semantics in <computeroutput>raze::vx</computeroutput></ref></para>
</listitem><listitem><para><ref refid="group__raze__options" kindref="compound">Options</ref></para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>raze::options::strategy_mode::autovec</computeroutput> </para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
    </detaileddescription>
    <location file="C:/Users/danya/source/repos/Midoritotoro/raze/src/raze/options/Traits.h"/>
  </compounddef>
</doxygen>

</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>proj</computeroutput> - projection to apply to elements (defaults to <computeroutput>std::identity</computeroutput>)</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>

<title>Return value</title><para>A <computeroutput>std::ranges::in_fun_result</computeroutput> containing:<itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><computeroutput>in</computeroutput>: an iterator pointing past the last processed element (<computeroutput>first + n</computeroutput> if <computeroutput>n &gt; 0</computeroutput>, otherwise <computeroutput>first</computeroutput>).</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>fun</computeroutput>: the function object <computeroutput>f</computeroutput> passed as an argument.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>

      <memberdef kind="variable" id="group__raze__algo_1gaa4a5eb02a0a73321a51c0394576d726c" prot="public" static="no" constexpr="yes" mutable="no">
        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto raze::algorithm::replace_copy_if</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>replace_copy_if</name>
        <qualifiedname>raze::algorithm::replace_copy_if</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Copies elements from a range to another range, replacing all elements equal to a given value with a new value. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>1) Copies elements from <computeroutput>[first, sent)</computeroutput> to the destination range beginning at <computeroutput>out</computeroutput>, replacing each element with <computeroutput>new_value</computeroutput> if <computeroutput>bool(std::invoke(proj, *i) == old_value)</computeroutput> evaluates to <computeroutput>true</computeroutput>.</para>
<para>2) Same as (1), but uses <computeroutput>r</computeroutput> as the source range, as if by: <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__algo_1gaf5de0fa419f2866715a88c5c70021b92" kindref="member">replace_copy</ref>(std::ranges::begin(r), std::ranges::end(r), std::move(out), old_value, new_value, proj)</computeroutput>.</para>

        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>replace_if</name>
        <qualifiedname>raze::algorithm::replace_if</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Replaces all elements satisfying a specific predicate in a range with a new value. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>1) Replaces each element <computeroutput>*i</computeroutput> in <computeroutput>[first, last)</computeroutput> with <computeroutput>new_value</computeroutput> if <computeroutput>bool(std::invoke(pred, std::invoke(proj, *i)))</computeroutput> evaluates to <computeroutput>true</computeroutput>.</para>
<para>2) Same as (1), but uses <computeroutput>r</computeroutput> as the source range, as if by: <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__algo_1ga9f2467e00689989f5e4fc2318303a74f" kindref="member">replace_if</ref>(std::ranges::begin(r), std::ranges::end(r), pred, new_value, proj)</computeroutput>.</para>

        <briefdescription>
<para>Exchanges elements between two ranges. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>1) Exchanges elements from the range <computeroutput>[first1, last1)</computeroutput> with elements from the range <computeroutput>[first2, last2)</computeroutput>, as if by <computeroutput>std::ranges::iter_swap(first1, first2)</computeroutput>. The exchange stops when either range reaches its end.</para>
<para>2) Same as (1), but uses <computeroutput>r1</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>r2</computeroutput> as the source ranges, as if by: <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__algo_1gaa74325f86200071527654294dd02e1b0" kindref="member">swap_ranges</ref>(std::ranges::begin(r1), std::ranges::end(r1), std::ranges::begin(r2), std::ranges::end(r2))</computeroutput>.</para>

<sect1 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md36_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md36_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md36">
<title>Notes</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Unlike <computeroutput>std::swap_ranges</computeroutput>, this algorithm safely accepts ranges of unequal lengths and processes elements up to the size of the smaller range.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>If both ranges model contiguous storage over the same trivially copyable value types, explicit SIMD vectorization (AVX-512, AVX2, SSE) or platform-specific autovectorization paths are utilized.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>In a constant-evaluated context, the algorithm executes via the scalar fallback path using <computeroutput>std::ranges::iter_swap</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>

      <memberdef kind="variable" id="group__raze__algo_1ga0478cc61f28c7bb7e527cc0c31017c27" prot="public" static="no" constexpr="yes" mutable="no">
        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto raze::algorithm::transform</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>transform</name>
        <qualifiedname>raze::algorithm::transform</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Applies a given function to a range (or a pair of ranges) and stores the result in another range. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>1) <bold>Unary transform (iterator-sentinel)</bold>: Applies the unary function <computeroutput>f</computeroutput> to each element in <computeroutput>[first, last)</computeroutput> projected by <computeroutput>proj</computeroutput>, and writes the results to the destination range beginning at <computeroutput>out</computeroutput>.</para>
<para>2) <bold>Unary transform (range)</bold>: Same as (1), but uses <computeroutput>r</computeroutput> as the input range, as if by: <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__algo_1ga0478cc61f28c7bb7e527cc0c31017c27" kindref="member">transform</ref>(std::ranges::begin(r), std::ranges::end(r), std::move(out), f, proj)</computeroutput>.</para>
<para>3) <bold>Binary transform (iterator-sentinel)</bold>: Applies the binary function <computeroutput>f</computeroutput> to pairs of elements from <computeroutput>[first1, last1)</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>[first2, last2)</computeroutput> projected by <computeroutput>proj1</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>proj2</computeroutput> respectively, and writes the results to <computeroutput>out</computeroutput>. Evaluation stops when either input range reaches its end.</para>
<para>4) <bold>Binary transform (range)</bold>: Same as (3), but uses <computeroutput>r1</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>r2</computeroutput> as the input ranges, as if by: <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__algo_1ga0478cc61f28c7bb7e527cc0c31017c27" kindref="member">transform</ref>(std::ranges::begin(r1), std::ranges::end(r1), std::ranges::begin(r2), std::ranges::end(r2), std::move(out), f, proj1, proj2)</computeroutput>.</para>
<sect1 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md59_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md59_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md59">

</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>out</computeroutput>: an iterator pointing past the last written element in the destination range.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>

</listitem><listitem><para>For <bold>binary overloads</bold> (3, 4): A <computeroutput>std::ranges::binary_transform_result</computeroutput> containing:<itemizedlist>

</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>out</computeroutput>: an iterator pointing past the last written element in the destination range.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>

<sect1 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md62_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md62_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md62">
<title>Complexity</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Unary: Exactly <computeroutput>last - first</computeroutput> (or <computeroutput>std::ranges::distance(r)</computeroutput>) invocations of <computeroutput>f</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>proj</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>Binary: Exactly <computeroutput>min(last1 - first1, last2 - first2)</computeroutput> (or <computeroutput>min(distance(r1), distance(r2))</computeroutput>) invocations of <computeroutput>f</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>proj1</computeroutput>, and <computeroutput>proj2</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>

<sect1 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md64_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md64_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__algo_1autotoc_md64">
<title>Notes</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Unlike <computeroutput>std::ranges::transform</computeroutput> for binary operations, this algorithm safely processes ranges of mismatched lengths up to the length of the shorter range.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>If sources and destinations model contiguous buffers, and user-provided functions/projections satisfy vectorization requirements, explicit SIMD instructions (AVX-512, AVX2, SSE) or platform-specific autovectorization paths are utilized.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>In a constant-evaluated context, the algorithm executes via the scalar fallback path.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>

  <compounddef id="group__raze__options" kind="group">
    <compoundname>raze_options</compoundname>
    <title>Options</title>
    <sectiondef kind="var">
      <memberdef kind="variable" id="group__raze__options_1ga6e41c5c8d3ba0dbed249b7d479100116" prot="public" static="no" constexpr="yes" mutable="no">
        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto fscalar</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>fscalar</name>
        <initializer>= raze::options::flag(fscalar_mode{})</initializer>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Option flag that forces scalar execution mode. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>When attached to an algorithm, <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__options_1ga6e41c5c8d3ba0dbed249b7d479100116" kindref="member">fscalar</ref></computeroutput> completely disables all SIMD hardware intrinsics (including compiler autovectorization) .</para>
<para>Forces the algorithm to execute using only standard scalar instructions and loops.</para>

        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto strict_types</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>strict_types</name>
        <initializer>= raze::options::flag(strict_types_mode{})</initializer>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Option flag that enforces strict input type matching for SIMD vectorization. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>By default, mixed-type binary algorithms (e.g., <computeroutput>transform</computeroutput>) allow SIMD vectorization of heterogeneous inputs (such as <computeroutput>int32_t</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>float</computeroutput>) by promoting both operands to their <computeroutput>std::common_type_t</computeroutput> before invoking the user-provided function. This mirrors standard scalar usual arithmetic conversions.</para>
<para>However, if the user-provided functor inspects the exact static type of its arguments (e.g., via <computeroutput>decltype</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>sizeof</computeroutput>, or type-specific overloads), this implicit common-type promotion may alter the intended semantics.</para>
<para>Attaching <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__options_1gaf4feab275d6c5651e07f125a098c4bf9" kindref="member">strict_types</ref></computeroutput> disables this promotion. The algorithm will only utilize the vectorized SIMD path if both input types are strictly identical. If the types differ, it safely falls back to the scalar execution path, guaranteeing 100% scalar-equivalent semantics.</para>
<sect1 id="group__raze__options_1autotoc_md83_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__options_1autotoc_md83_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__options_1autotoc_md83">

        <templateparamlist>
          <param>
            <type>arithmetic_type</type>
            <declname>T</declname>

        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto raze::vx::convert</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>convert</name>
        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::convert</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Converts every lane of a SIMD vector to a different arithmetic type, with conditional pass-through for unsupported types. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Returns a SIMD vector of type <computeroutput><ref refid="classraze_1_1vx_1_1simd" kindref="compound">simd</ref>&lt;T, V::abi_type&gt;</computeroutput> where each lane is converted from the source element type to the destination type <computeroutput>T</computeroutput>.</para>
<para>By default, standard C++ <computeroutput>static_cast</computeroutput> semantics are used (truncation). If the <computeroutput>raze::vx::saturated</computeroutput> option is attached, conversions are clamped to the destination type&apos;s limits.</para>
<para>If the <computeroutput>raze::vx::ignore_unsupported</computeroutput> option is attached and the types are <bold>not</bold> arithmetic (i.e., unsupported by standard conversion), the function acts as an identity function, returning the input vector <computeroutput>x</computeroutput> unchanged (bit-wise). However, if <computeroutput>[raze::vx::ignore_unsupported]</computeroutput> is provided but the types <emphasis>are</emphasis> arithmetic, the normal conversion (or saturated conversion) is still performed. This allows generic algorithms to use a unified code path for both arithmetic types and raw <computeroutput>trivially_copyable</computeroutput> types.</para>
<sect1 id="group__raze__vx__arith_1autotoc_md144_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__vx__arith_1autotoc_md144_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__vx__arith_1autotoc_md144">
<title>Saturation semantics</title><para>When <computeroutput>[raze::vx::saturated]</computeroutput> is used (and types are arithmetic), the conversion follows these rules:<itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>Float to Integer</bold>: <computeroutput>NaN</computeroutput> becomes <computeroutput>0</computeroutput>. Values out of bounds are clamped to <computeroutput>min</computeroutput>/<computeroutput>max</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Float to Float (narrowing)</bold>: <computeroutput>NaN</computeroutput> remains <computeroutput>NaN</computeroutput>. Out-of-bounds values are clamped.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Integer to Integer (narrowing)</bold>: Out-of-bounds values are clamped to <computeroutput>min</computeroutput>/<computeroutput>max</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Signed to Unsigned</bold>: Negative values become <computeroutput>0</computeroutput>. Values exceeding <computeroutput>max</computeroutput> are clamped.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Unsigned to Signed</bold>: Values exceeding <computeroutput>max</computeroutput> are clamped.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="group__raze__vx__arith_1autotoc_md145_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__vx__arith_1autotoc_md145_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__vx__arith_1autotoc_md145">
<title>Declarations</title><para><programlisting filename=".cpp"><codeline><highlight class="keyword">template</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>&lt;</highlight><highlight class="keyword">typename</highlight><highlight class="normal"><sp/>T&gt;</highlight></codeline>

</programlisting></para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>

        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::as_ternary_mask</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Generates an 8-bit truth table immediate for <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__vx__bitwise_1ga4ce0c005439d7e10a31afc26f9cf1df4" kindref="member">ternarylogic</ref></computeroutput> from a compile-time logical expression. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Allows constructing the <computeroutput>Op</computeroutput> immediate required by <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__vx__bitwise_1ga4ce0c005439d7e10a31afc26f9cf1df4" kindref="member">ternarylogic</ref></computeroutput> using standard logical operators (<computeroutput>&amp;</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>|</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>^</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>~</computeroutput>) over the symbolic variables <computeroutput>raze::vx::A</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>raze::vx::B</computeroutput>, and <computeroutput>raze::vx::C</computeroutput>. The expression is evaluated for all 8 input combinations at compile time to compute the truth table.</para>

        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::bit_shr</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Computes the element-wise bitwise right shift of a SIMD vector. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Shifts every lane right by <computeroutput>shift</computeroutput> bits: <computeroutput>out[i] = x[i] &gt;&gt; shift</computeroutput>.</para>
<para><bold>Semantics:</bold><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Unsigned <computeroutput>value_type</computeroutput>: logical shift.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>Signed <computeroutput>value_type</computeroutput>: arithmetic shift.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>If <computeroutput>shift &gt;= bit_width(value_type)</computeroutput>, the result is zero (unsigned) or sign-extended (signed).</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>

<title>Mask semantics</title><para>Supports <bold>only</bold> the maskz form (<computeroutput>[m]</computeroutput>). If the mask <computeroutput>m[i]</computeroutput> is <computeroutput>false</computeroutput>, the corresponding lane in the resulting <computeroutput><ref refid="classsimd__mask" kindref="compound">simd_mask</ref></computeroutput> is <computeroutput>false</computeroutput>.</para>
<para><bold>Merge semantics (<computeroutput>[m, src]</computeroutput>) are not supported</bold> because the result type is a mask, not a vector.</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>

=== group__raze__vx__mask__reduce.xml ===
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='no'?>
<doxygen xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="compound.xsd" version="1.18.0" xml:lang="en-US">
  <compounddef id="group__raze__vx__mask__reduce" kind="group">
    <compoundname>raze_vx_mask_reduce</compoundname>
    <title>Mask Reductions</title>
    <sectiondef kind="var">
      <memberdef kind="variable" id="group__raze__vx__mask__reduce_1ga8d924d205cc62087e8c69251e037e8fd" prot="public" static="no" constexpr="yes" mutable="no">
        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto raze::vx::all_of</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>all_of</name>
        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::all_of</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Checks if all active lanes of a SIMD mask are <computeroutput>true</computeroutput>. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Returns <computeroutput>true</computeroutput> if every active lane in the input mask <computeroutput>x</computeroutput> evaluates to <computeroutput>true</computeroutput>. If the mask is entirely <computeroutput>false</computeroutput>, the result is <computeroutput>true</computeroutput>. Also accepts <computeroutput>algorithm::tail_mask_type</computeroutput> by delegating to its underlying mask.</para>
<sect1 id="group__raze__vx__mask__reduce_1autotoc_md246_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__vx__mask__reduce_1autotoc_md246_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__vx__mask__reduce_1autotoc_md246">

      <memberdef kind="variable" id="group__raze__vx__memory_1gadc629e089bc40a0a7803b4fedd1b0f5b" prot="public" static="no" constexpr="yes" mutable="no">
        <type>auto</type>
        <definition>auto raze::vx::compress_store</definition>
        <argsstring></argsstring>
        <name>compress_store</name>
        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::compress_store</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Compresses elements from a SIMD vector into contiguous memory according to a mask. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Writes elements of <computeroutput>x</computeroutput> to the memory location starting at <computeroutput>it</computeroutput> for every lane where <computeroutput>mask[i]</computeroutput> evaluates to <computeroutput>false</computeroutput>. The target memory must be large enough to hold the compressed elements.</para>
<sect1 id="group__raze__vx__memory_1autotoc_md204_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__vx__memory_1autotoc_md204_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__vx__memory_1autotoc_md204">
<title>Options</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><computeroutput>raze::vx::unsafe</computeroutput> — Enables a faster store operation. When provided, the trailing memory region <computeroutput>[it + <ref refid="group__raze__vx__mask__reduce_1ga563a3750c9979e08eb6f21ab5763e297" kindref="member">count_set</ref>(!mask), it + V::size())</computeroutput> is filled with garbage. By default, these trailing elements are left unchanged.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>raze::vx::aligned</computeroutput> — Uses aligned memory stores.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="group__raze__vx__memory_1autotoc_md205_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__vx__memory_1autotoc_md205_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__vx__memory_1autotoc_md205">

        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::slide_right_merge</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Shifts the elements of a SIMD vector to the right, filling the leftmost lanes with elements from another vector. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Shifts the elements of <computeroutput>x</computeroutput> to the right by <computeroutput>i</computeroutput> positions. The rightmost elements are discarded, and the leftmost <computeroutput>i</computeroutput> lanes are filled with the last <computeroutput>i</computeroutput> elements of <computeroutput>y</computeroutput>. The shift amount can be passed either as a runtime integer or a compile-time <computeroutput>std::integral_constant</computeroutput>.</para>

        <qualifiedname>raze::vx::swap_adjacent</qualifiedname>
        <briefdescription>
<para>Swaps adjacent blocks of elements within a SIMD vector. </para>
        </briefdescription>
        <detaileddescription>
<para>Partitions the input vector <computeroutput>x</computeroutput> into contiguous blocks of size <computeroutput>2 * GroupSize</computeroutput> and swaps the two halves within each block. If the vector size is not a multiple of <computeroutput>2 * GroupSize</computeroutput>, the last block is truncated, but the swap logic is applied as if the pattern wraps around.</para>
<sect1 id="group__raze__vx__shuffle_1autotoc_md420_1s1"><sect2 id="group__raze__vx__shuffle_1autotoc_md420_1s2"><sect3 id="group__raze__vx__shuffle_1autotoc_md420">

        <definition>using raze::vx::make_swap_adjacent_pattern = make_shuffle_pattern&lt;V,
   [] (sizetype i) {
       constexpr auto block = 2 * GroupSize;

       const auto block_begin = (i / block) * block;
       const auto offset = i % block;

       auto index = 0;

       if (offset &lt; GroupSize) index = block_begin + offset + GroupSize;
       else index = block_begin + offset - GroupSize;

=== mask_semantics.xml ===
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='no'?>
<doxygen xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="compound.xsd" version="1.18.0" xml:lang="en-US">
  <compounddef id="mask_semantics" kind="page">
    <compoundname>mask_semantics</compoundname>
    <title>Mask semantics in &lt;tt&gt;raze::vx&lt;/tt&gt;</title>
    <briefdescription>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para>Most configurable primitives in <computeroutput>raze::vx</computeroutput> — <computeroutput>broadcast</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>all_bits</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>zero</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>add</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>sub</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>mul</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>div</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>select</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>load</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>store</computeroutput>, and their friends — accept mask modifiers through <computeroutput>operator[]</computeroutput>. This page describes those modifiers once; individual primitive pages only list which forms they support and link here.</para>
<sect1 id="mask_semantics_1autotoc_md73_1s1"><sect2 id="mask_semantics_1autotoc_md73_1s2"><sect3 id="mask_semantics_1autotoc_md73">
<title>Call forms</title><para>For a primitive <computeroutput>op</computeroutput> (a <computeroutput>options::functor</computeroutput>):</para>
<para><programlisting filename=".cpp"><codeline><highlight class="normal">op(...);<sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/></highlight><highlight class="comment">//<sp/>(1)<sp/>unmasked</highlight><highlight class="normal"></highlight></codeline>
<codeline><highlight class="normal">op[m](...);<sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/></highlight><highlight class="comment">//<sp/>(2)<sp/>maskz</highlight><highlight class="normal"></highlight></codeline>
<codeline><highlight class="normal">op[m,<sp/>src](...);<sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/></highlight><highlight class="comment">//<sp/>(3)<sp/>merge</highlight><highlight class="normal"></highlight></codeline>
<codeline><highlight class="normal">op[src,<sp/>m](...);<sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/><sp/></highlight><highlight class="comment">//<sp/>(3&apos;)<sp/>merge,<sp/>arguments<sp/>in<sp/>any<sp/>order</highlight></codeline>
</programlisting></para>
<para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>Unmasked (1)</bold> — every lane receives the primitive&apos;s natural result.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Maskz (2)</bold> — lane <computeroutput>i</computeroutput> receives the result if <computeroutput>m</computeroutput> selects it, else the lane is zeroed.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><bold>Merge (3)/(3&apos;)</bold> — lane <computeroutput>i</computeroutput> receives the result if <computeroutput>m</computeroutput> selects it, else <computeroutput>src[i]</computeroutput>. <computeroutput>m</computeroutput> and <computeroutput>src</computeroutput> may be given in either order; both overloads normalize to the same <computeroutput>or_(m, src)</computeroutput> expression. </para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="mask_semantics_1autotoc_md74_1s1"><sect2 id="mask_semantics_1autotoc_md74_1s2"><sect3 id="mask_semantics_1autotoc_md74">
<title>Low-level equivalence</title><para>This is mostly useful inside generic code that builds conditions dynamically; ordinary call sites should use the <computeroutput>[m]</computeroutput> / <computeroutput>[m, src]</computeroutput> shorthands. </para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
    </detaileddescription>
    <location file="raze/vx/Mask.h"/>
  </compounddef>
</doxygen>

      </memberdef>
    </sectiondef>
    <briefdescription>
<para>ABI descriptor enabling runtime‑dispatched SIMD execution on MSVC. </para>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para><parameterlist kind="templateparam"><parameteritem>
<parameternamelist>
<parametername>ISA</parametername>
</parameternamelist>
<parameterdescription>
<para>Maximum instruction set architecture that the dispatcher is permitted to use. </para>
</parameterdescription>
</parameteritem>
<parameteritem>
<parameternamelist>
<parametername>Width</parametername>
</parameternamelist>
<parameterdescription>
<para>SIMD register width in bits. Defaults to the natural width of <computeroutput>ISA</computeroutput>.</para>
</parameterdescription>
</parameteritem>
</parameterlist>
This ABI model is intended **exclusively for MSVC compiler. It does not perform instruction selection by itself. Instead, it is designed to be used together with an external runtime dispatcher that selects the most capable SIMD implementation available on the current CPU.</para>
<para>The purpose of this ABI is to allow MSVC builds to store <bold>all SIMD implementations in a single binary</bold> without incurring the performance penalties normally associated with dynamic dispatch. Since these compilers do not support compile‑time multiversioning (such as <computeroutput>target_clones</computeroutput>, <computeroutput>target</computeroutput> attributes), a dedicated runtime dispatcher is required to route SIMD operations to the appropriate ISA‑specific code path.</para>
<para>On GCC and Clang, this ABI model is <bold>not applicable</bold>. True runtime ISA dispatch on those compilers requires compiling multiple translation units with different simd flags and loading them dynamically (e.g., via <computeroutput>dlopen</computeroutput>). For GCC/Clang, use the regular <computeroutput>fixed_abi</computeroutput> with compile‑time ISA selection instead.</para>
<para>In summary:<itemizedlist>
<listitem><para>Use <computeroutput><ref refid="structraze_1_1vx_1_1runtime__abi" kindref="compound">runtime_abi</ref></computeroutput> on <bold>MSVC</bold> together with a runtime dispatcher.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para>Use <computeroutput>fixed_abi</computeroutput> on <bold>GCC/Clang</bold> for compile‑time ISA selection.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
<para>This ABI descriptor exposes basic architectural properties such as register width and register count, enabling the dispatcher to construct and manage ISA‑specific SIMD backends efficiently. </para>
    </detaileddescription>

    </sectiondef>
    <briefdescription>
<para>A compile-time descriptor for SIMD element permutations. </para>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para><computeroutput><ref refid="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern" kindref="compound">shuffle_pattern</ref>&lt;V, Idxs...&gt;</computeroutput> describes how to rearrange the elements of a SIMD vector of type <computeroutput>V</computeroutput>. It acts as a strongly-typed, compile-time array of source indices.</para>
<para>The pattern holds a sequence of indices <computeroutput>Idxs...</computeroutput>. When applied via <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__vx__shuffle_1gaec90c7acc83a1f67613f093ceda8d626" kindref="member">raze::vx::shuffle</ref></computeroutput>, lane <computeroutput>i</computeroutput> of the result receives the value from lane <computeroutput>Idxs[i]</computeroutput> of the input. If an index equals <computeroutput><ref refid="group__raze__vx__shuffle__patterns_1ga13b5509cfbca60e032693d17c459ffca" kindref="member">raze::vx::shuffle_zero</ref></computeroutput> (or <computeroutput>-1</computeroutput>), the resulting lane is filled with zeros.</para>
<sect1 id="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern_1autotoc_md91_1s1"><sect2 id="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern_1autotoc_md91_1s2"><sect3 id="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern_1autotoc_md91">
<title>Key Characteristics</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><bold>Compile-time</bold>: All index checking and pattern analysis happens during compilation.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
<sect1 id="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern_1autotoc_md92_1s1"><sect2 id="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern_1autotoc_md92_1s2"><sect3 id="structraze_1_1vx_1_1shuffle__pattern_1autotoc_md92">
<title>Template Parameters</title><para><itemizedlist>
<listitem><para><computeroutput>V</computeroutput> — The target SIMD type.</para>
</listitem><listitem><para><computeroutput>Idxs...</computeroutput> — The sequence of source indices. The number of indices must equal <computeroutput>V::size()</computeroutput>.</para>
</listitem></itemizedlist>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>

=== supported_arch.xml ===
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='no'?>
<doxygen xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="compound.xsd" version="1.18.0" xml:lang="en-US">
  <compounddef id="supported_arch" kind="page">
    <compoundname>supported_arch</compoundname>
    <title>Supported Architectures</title>
    <briefdescription>
    </briefdescription>
    <detaileddescription>
<para>RAZE is optimized for the x86 (and x86-64) architecture. The library automatically detects and adapts to the host CPU&apos;s capabilities, utilizing the most advanced instruction sets available at compile time or runtime (see <ref refid="dynamic_dispatch" kindref="compound">Dynamic dispatch in <computeroutput>raze::algorithm</computeroutput></ref>).</para>
<para>The minimum supported architecture is <bold>SSE2</bold> (the x86-64 baseline).</para>
<sect1 id="supported_arch_1autotoc_md427_1s1"><sect2 id="supported_arch_1autotoc_md427_1s2"><sect3 id="supported_arch_1autotoc_md427">
<title>Supported Instruction Sets</title><para>The following ISA extensions are fully supported and utilized by the backend:</para>
<para><table rows="4" cols="2"><row>
<entry thead="yes" align='left'><para>Family  </para>
</entry><entry thead="yes" align='left'><para>Supported Extensions  </para>
</entry></row>
<row>
<entry thead="no" align='left'><para><bold>SSE</bold>  </para>
</entry><entry thead="no" align='left'><para>SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2  </para>
</entry></row>
<row>
<entry thead="no" align='left'><para><bold>AVX</bold>  </para>
</entry><entry thead="no" align='left'><para>AVX, AVX2, FMA3  </para>
</entry></row>
<row>
<entry thead="no" align='left'><para><bold>AVX-512</bold>  </para>
</entry><entry thead="no" align='left'><para>AVX512F, AVX512VL, AVX512BW, AVX512DQ, AVX512VBMI, AVX512VBMI2  </para>
</entry></row>
</table>
</para>
</sect3></sect2></sect1>
